title: Applied ML Eval Harness and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook describes Redwood's Applied ML evaluation (eval) harness, the prompt sets and benchmark standards we use for onboarding and regression detection, our quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and the regression triage process. The goal is to ensure model changes and infra/quantization updates maintain customer-facing quality SLOs while enabling safe performance and cost optimizations.

Scope:
- Applicable to all model onboarding flows (open models and internal variants) and to runtime/quantization changes that may affect output quality.
- Covers evaluation automation (eval-harness), prompt set curation, benchmark baselines, automatic/regression alerting, and incident/ticket playbooks for triage.

Key owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: Applied ML (engineering)  Aisha Patel
- Eval harness service: eval-service (infra owner: Eng Serving Runtime)
- On-call escalation: Applied ML rotation (see eng-sre/oncall roster)

1) Eval harness architecture and expectations
- Components:
  - eval-runner: orchestrates batch evals, supports per-model jobs, metrics export to metrics-store.
  - prompt-store: canonical prompt sets with metadata and tags (domain, difficulty, negative-cases).
  - threshold-engine: compares new results to baseline and emits regression alerts.
  - artifacts: outputs (predictions, scores, diff reports) stored in s3://redwood-evals/artefacts/{model}/{run}.
- SLAs and cadence:
  1. Onboarding full-suite run: completed within 24 hours of job kickoff (target).
  2. Nightly smoke/regression runs for released models: complete delta check within 2 hours of job completion, alerts emitted if any metric crosses thresholds.
  3. Eval data retention: raw outputs retained 180 days; aggregated metrics retained 3 years.

2) Prompt sets and benchmark design guidelines
- Prompt set tiers:
  - Tier 0 (smoke): 50 representative prompts, focused on safety and basic correctness. Used for quick pre-release checks.
  - Tier 1 (core benchmarks): 500-1,000 prompts covering key verticals (summarization, completion, instruction-following, embeddings similarity).
  - Tier 2 (stress/edge): 5k+ prompts including adversarial and long-context cases used for deeper regression analysis and quantization stress tests.
- Curation rules:
  - Every prompt has metadata: intent, expected outputs (if applicable), difficulty, and failure-mode tags.
  - Create balanced sets: at least 4 vendors/annotators per label for labeled prompts.
  - Maintain a changelog for prompt set edits; require peer review for deletions or label changes.
- Benchmarks and metrics:
  - Metrics: BLEU/ROUGE for summarization tasks, exact-match/F1 for closed QA, embedding cosine AUC for similarity, and human-rated quality (1-5) for open-generation tasks.
  - Primary quality SLO: production models must not regress >2.0% absolute on primary metric across Tier 1 vs baseline without explicit sign-off. Secondary metrics allow 5% drift before manual review.

3) Model onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1. Initial model artifacts: upload model weights and manifest to model-registry with SHA256 and provenance.
2. Baseline registration: select baseline model (most recent GA) and record baseline metrics across Tier 1 and Tier 2.
3. Eval harness run: schedule full-suite eval (Tier 0-2).
4. Quantization smoke: run quantization profile test (see section 5) on representative subset; compare logits/decoded outputs to fp16 baseline.
5. Safety and toxicity checks: run safety classifiers and policy filters; require zero high-severity safety violations for public release.
6. Performance profiling: run latency and throughput benches at 95th-percentile request size; record in model metadata.
7. Review: Applied ML + product stake sign-off for release. If any metric crosses regression thresholds, follow regression triage flow.

4) Quality guardrails and automated checks
- Automated pre-commit checks in eval-runner:
  - Token-level sanity checks (length distributions, tokenization errors).
  - Output format validation (JSON schema for structured outputs).
  - Safety classifier pass/fail with severity tags.
- Policy for acceptable changes:
  - Minor improvements (improve primary metric and no safety failures) are auto-approvable.
  - Small regressions (<1% abs on primary metric) require reviewer approval but may be allowed if accompanied by explainable trade-off (e.g., latency improvement).
  - Regressions >=2% or any high-severity safety violation block release automatically.

5) Quantization profiles and validation
- Profiles maintained in quant-profiles/ (example: gptx-8bit-perf, gptx-4bit-accuracy). Each profile includes: algorithm, bitwidth, blocked-layers, calibration-data-id, validation-suite-id.
- Validation steps:
  1. Run functional diff against fp16 baseline on Tier 1 (full pass) and Tier 2 subset (stress).
  2. Compute metric deltas and token-level divergence (KL, top-k overlap).
  3. Run targeted human evaluation on 200 samples where automated metrics indicate >0.5% delta on primary metric.
  4. If human eval or automated metrics exceed tolerance, mark profile as "restricted" and attach notes.
- Gates:
  - 8-bit profiles: allowed for dedicated/hosted use with standard review if primary metric drift <1.5% and no safety regressions.
  - 4-bit aggressive profiles: require full Applied ML sign-off and customer communication; default to restricted for enterprise/private deployments unless explicitly approved.

6) Regression detection and triage playbook
- Alerting:
  - threshold-engine emits alerts to #applied-ml-regressions with embedded diff reports and top failing prompts.
  - Pager triggered only for high-severity regressions or safety failures.
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1. Triage owner acknowledges alert within 15 minutes.
  2. Reproduce: rerun the failing eval suite to rule out transient infra issues.
  3. Narrow: identify whether regression is model, quantization, runtime (kernel), or data change. Use artifacts: logits, token overlap, perf traces.
  4. Mitigate: if regression is quantization, rollback profile or pin to fp16; if model change, rollback to baseline or deploy canary with reduced traffic.
  5. Resolve: create a postmortem if customer impact occurred or regression >2% on primary metric.
  6. Prevent: add targeted tests to Tier 1 and update prompt sets to cover the failure mode.
- Triage playbook checklist (for incident ticket):
  - Repro steps and datasets used (pointer to artifacts).
  - Summary table: metric, baseline, new, delta, severity.
  - Owner and timeline of changes (git commit, deployment id).
  - Mitigation enacted and time-to-fix.

7) Rollout patterns and safe deploys
- Canary: 1% traffic for 24 hours with continuous Tier 0 smoke checks in prod.
- A/B: split 10/90 for 48 hours with automated statistical test on primary metric.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to baseline model variant on error-rate >1% or primary metric drop >2.0% in 1 hour window.

8) Reporting, dashboards and artifact links
- Dashboards:
  - Per-model: primary metric trend, Tier 1 pass-rate, nightly-regression status, latency P50/P95.
  - Quantization: per-profile diffs and flagged prompts.
- Artifact links for triage are always included in alert messages (s3 path and run id). Standard naming: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{model}/{YYYYMMDDHHMM}_{run-id}/

Appendix A - Example eval-runner job YAML
---
job_name: "onboard-gptx-v2-full-suite"
model: "gptx-v2"
baseline: "gptx-v1"
prompt_sets: ["tier0-smoke", "tier1-core", "tier2-stress-sample"]
quant_profile: "gptx-8bit-perf"
notify_channel: "#applied-ml-regressions"
expected_max_run_time: "24h"
---

Appendix B - Quick runbook (condensed)
1) Acknowledge and reproduce reg: rerun eval-runner with --run-id <original> --replay
2) If reproduced and metric delta >2%: open ticket and assign Sev-2, notify Product and SRE.
3) If quantization suspected: revert to fp16 profile and re-run smoke; if passes, schedule re-quantization with expanded calibration data.
